items.followUp: Define friction and write two ways to increase it.

rubric.why: Friction is defined by the motion it opposes and the surfaces between which it acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that friction opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact.

rubric.why: A lubricant reduces friction between surfaces.
rubric.description: Names lubrication as a method of reducing friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a lubricant, such as oil or grease.

rubric.why: Polishing or smoothing reduces surface irregularities and friction.
rubric.description: Names polishing or smoothing as a method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that polishing or smoothing the surfaces reduces friction.

rubric.why: Ball bearings or rollers reduce friction by replacing sliding with rolling.
rubric.description: Names ball bearings or rollers as a method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning ball bearings or rollers.

modelAnswer: Friction is the force that opposes the relative motion, or tendency of relative motion, between two surfaces in contact.
Friction can be reduced by applying a lubricant such as oil or grease.
Friction can be reduced by polishing or smoothing the surfaces.
Friction can be reduced by using ball bearings or rollers.

items.followUp: A force of 50 N makes an angle of 30° with the positive x-axis. Find its perpendicular x- and y-components.

rubric.why: The component equations use the angle measured from the positive x-axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that θ is measured from the positive x-axis.

rubric.why: The x-component is the projection of F along the x-axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Fx = F cos θ.

rubric.why: The y-component is the projection of F along the y-axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Fy = F sin θ.

rubric.why: The components act along mutually perpendicular axes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the x- and y-components are perpendicular.

modelAnswer: Let θ (theta) be the angle between vector F and the positive x-axis.
The perpendicular x-component is Fx = F cos θ.
The perpendicular y-component is Fy = F sin θ.
These components act along the mutually perpendicular x- and y-axes.

items.followUp: A ball of mass 200 g moves at 10 m s⁻¹. Calculate its kinetic energy.

rubric.why: Mass must be expressed in kilograms for SI substitution.
rubric.description: Converts the mass to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining m = 0.5 kg from 500 g.

rubric.why: Correct substitution uses the converted mass and the given speed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting 0.5 kg and 20 m s⁻¹ into the formula.

rubric.why: Evaluating the substitution gives a numerical value of 100.
The SI unit of kinetic energy is the joule.
rubric.description: Gives the final answer with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating KE = 100 J.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 500 g = 0.5 kg, v = 20 m s⁻¹.

items.followUp: Write four properties of a suitable thermometric liquid.

rubric.why: Uniform expansion gives a reliable temperature scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that the liquid expands uniformly with temperature.

rubric.why: The liquid should not cling to the thermometer glass.
rubric.description: States that it does not wet or stick to glass.

rubric.why: A low freezing point allows the liquid to measure low temperatures.
rubric.description: States that it has a low freezing point.

rubric.why: A high boiling point allows the liquid to measure higher temperatures.
rubric.description: States that it has a high boiling point.

modelAnswer: A thermometric liquid should expand uniformly with temperature.
It should not wet or stick to the glass of the thermometer.
It should have a low freezing point.
It should have a high boiling point.
